name: spacecraft
description: Anything that flies in space: a rocket, a satellite or a spaceship.
conventions: Engines and thrusters are separate nodes with their pivot at the nozzle throat, so an effect and a thrust direction can sit on them.
A craft that is landed stands on y = 0 on its legs or its engines; in orbit there is no up, so the model keeps +Y as its top.
anticipate: A marker for each thruster (position and direction) for particle effects and for a physics script.
Emissive materials for lights and engine glow.
pitfalls: Engines baked into the hull cannot gimbal or glow on their own.
A spacecraft with no scale references (a door, a window) reads as a toy.

name: rocket
description: A launch vehicle: a tall cylinder with a nose cone, stages, engines at the bottom and fins or legs.

parts.name: NoseCone
parts.note: The pointed top: a cone, an ogive or a capsule with an escape tower.

parts.name: Engine
parts.note: At the bottom, in a ring or a cluster; the nozzle bell flares downward.

scale.source: public data: Falcon 9 about 70 m x 3.7 m, Saturn V about 110 m x 10 m; sounding rockets are shorter

conventions: A rocket stands upright on y = 0, its axis along y; the nozzle at the bottom, the nose cone at the top.
anticipate: The stages as separate nodes, so a stage can separate and fall away.
A marker at each nozzle for the flame effect, and a thin cylinder for the plume if it is meshed.
pitfalls: A rocket modelled lying along z: it stands on y = 0, upright.
Engines the width of the stage: the bells are smaller than the tank and tuck under it.

name: spaceship
description: A crewed science-fiction ship: a hull, a cockpit or bridge, engines at the back, often wings and landing gear.

parts.name: Cockpit
parts.note: Glazing or a bridge window at the front (+Z).

parts.name: LandingGear
parts.note: Hinged where the leg meets the hull, so it retracts.

scale.source: fiction: there is no real size; a wide range that only catches unit mistakes

anticipate: Engine glow as an emissive material, and a marker per engine for the exhaust effect.
Landing gear that retracts: separate nodes with a hinge pivot.
pitfalls: A hull that is one lump with details painted on: add panels, cockpit and engine bells as parts.
Left and right halves that differ by accident: mirror them exactly unless the ship is asymmetric on purpose.

name: satellite
description: A satellite or space probe: a body (the bus), two solar panels, and antennas or dishes.

parts.name: SolarPanel
parts.note: Hinged at the bus, so the panels can unfold or turn to the sun.

scale.source: general knowledge: small satellites a metre across to large stations (the ISS is about 109 m wide)

anticipate: Solar panels as separate nodes that can turn to the sun.
pitfalls: Panels as one fused wing: each panel is its own node so it can fold.
